package_info.why_malicious: Version 6.11.2 of the protobufjs package contains multiple prototype pollution vulnerabilities. These flaws allow untrusted input to modify object prototypes via exposed functions, such as util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, and the parsing/loading of .proto files. This can result in arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, or security bypasses in applications that process user-controlled data or files with this package.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code calls util.setProperty with user-controlled property names, allowing assignment to the __proto__ property of an object, resulting in prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function allows direct assignment to the __proto__ property using untrusted input, enabling attackers to pollute the prototype chain and potentially alter application logic or escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal usage expects input sanitization to prevent prototype modification; this code fails to restrict dangerous property names like __proto__, violating secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use involves setting object properties, but never prototype-related keys such as __proto__ from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: No sanitization of property names in util.setProperty
User-controlled property names passed to object assignment

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code invokes setParsedOption with untrusted input as the property name, enabling modification of the __proto__ property and causing prototype pollution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setParsedOption accepts user-controlled property names without filtering, allowing attackers to set prototype properties and compromise object integrity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to restrict prototype-related keys from being set via user input; this code does not enforce such restrictions, exposing the application to prototype pollution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Setting options on objects is common, but prototype keys like __proto__ should always be filtered out from user input.
key_indicators: Untrusted input used as property name in setParsedOption
Ability to set __proto__ via API call

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code parses a .proto definition containing prototype-polluting assignments from untrusted input, resulting in modification of object prototypes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Parsing untrusted .proto definitions without sanitizing property names allows attackers to inject prototype-polluting keys, leading to application compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to validate and sanitize .proto definitions before parsing; this code does not, allowing prototype pollution via crafted .proto files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parsing .proto files is legitimate, but only when the files are from trusted sources and property names are validated.
key_indicators: No sanitization of property names in .proto definitions
Ability to inject __proto__ assignments via .proto files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads and parses an untrusted .proto file, which may contain prototype-polluting definitions, resulting in prototype pollution of application objects.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and parsing untrusted .proto files without validation enables attackers to exploit prototype pollution vulnerabilities present in the parsing logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to only load trusted .proto files or to sanitize their contents before parsing; this code does neither, exposing the application to prototype pollution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Loading .proto files is normal, but only from trusted sources and with validation of file contents.
key_indicators: No validation or sanitization of .proto file contents
Potential for prototype-polluting definitions in loaded files

attack_chain.action: Attacker supplies untrusted input (arguments or files) to vulnerable protobufjs functions, such as util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, parse, or load.
Prototype pollution alters application behavior or enables further exploitation, such as privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full compromise of the application.

behavioral_signatures: Assignment to __proto__ or constructor.prototype via user input in object property assignment
Parsing or loading untrusted .proto files without property name sanitization
User-controlled property names passed to util.setProperty or setParsedOption
file_indicators: References to util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, parse, or load in protobufjs source code
Loading or parsing of .proto files from untrusted or user-supplied locations
network_indicators: N/A (vulnerability is local, but exploitation may involve remote delivery of malicious .proto files or user input)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for usage of vulnerable protobufjs functions (util.setProperty, ReflectionObject.setParsedOption, parse, load) where property names are derived from untrusted input, especially if they include '__proto__' or similar prototype-related keys. Flag any code paths where .proto files are loaded or parsed from user-supplied or untrusted sources. Use static analysis to detect assignment to prototype properties from user-controlled data, and audit file access patterns for loading .proto files from non-whitelisted locations.
